paragraphs.text: Marshall and Genie Loeb have given $1 million toward a new cancer center at the University of Mississippi Medical Center in Jackson. Marshall Loeb, whose sister Freddie Watson died of lymphoma, said her experience helped draw him to the project. UMMC announced the gift Nov. 16.

The Loebs’ gift goes to a $125 million fundraising campaign that helps pay for construction. UMMC broke ground Oct. 22. The campaign had already passed 80% of its goal by the groundbreaking, the medical center reported at the time. Sandy and John Black helped launch it with a $25 million gift.

For patients who travel to Jackson, one planned change is the chance to see several specialists in a single visit. UMMC’s design calls for clinics where the care team can meet with a patient together. A resource center open to the public, a chapel and rooms for patient and family support groups are planned for the main floor.

The building will also house infusion suites, research labs and space for clinical trials. UMMC is pursuing National Cancer Institute designation, which would be a first for Mississippi. The designation is a goal for the center as construction gets underway.
